confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from three web searches. These covered the Numbeo Marmaris cost-of-living page dated October 2026 (inexpensive meal about TRY 500, mid-range meal for two about TRY 2,150, cappuccino about TRY 177, domestic draft beer about TRY 150), Wise figures in GBP (about GBP 7 for an inexpensive meal and GBP 31 for a mid-range meal for two), and Marmaris drink guides from 2026. Those guides list a 50cl local beer at GBP 2.50-3.50 at the beachfront and more on Bar Street, standard cocktails at GBP 5-12, and a glass of wine at TRY 180-300. I converted lira prices at an approximate USD/TRY rate of 46-48 for mid-2026, which I inferred from Numbeo's EUR comparison, not from an official TRY source. I raised the beer and meal anchors slightly for July high season in tourist-area restaurants. The lira is volatile and prices vary a lot by venue (Bar Street and the marina cost more than backstreet places), so beer, cocktail and wine are less certain than meal and coffee. The cocktail anchor sits between one local price list (about TRY 225) and guide ranges in GBP (GBP 5-12). Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for July peak season, made without searches. Marmaris has few registered hostels, so the dorm and private-room anchors are especially uncertain. Many 3-star hotels there sell all-inclusive packages, so the 3-star anchor approximates a room-only rate.
comparable_city_reasoning: Searched prices are specific to Marmaris. For accommodation and the drinks premium in peak season, I used other Turkish Aegean and Mediterranean resort towns as comparables: Bodrum is more expensive, while Fethiye and Kusadasi are similar or slightly cheaper.
